prompt: A Cortex-M4 telemetry board latches a fault during the factory calibration read at boot, before any packet is streamed. The workspace holds the board source, the build and capture tools, the record the target wrote in faults/fault-1.txt, and the matching image with symbols in faults/fault-1.elf. Triage it from that record rather than by reflashing: decode the fault status registers, decide which fault address registers are valid and what they name, and resolve the stacked PC and LR against the matching ELF to the exact function and call site. Then decide whether the recorded instruction caused the fault or only surfaced it, repair firmware/board.c so the calibration read completes and the board streams its packets, and record the triage in diagnosis.json in the shape the README specifies. The harness rebuilds your source with a fresh seed and runs it on the target, so the published checksum has to come from the repaired packet path actually executing.

requirements: real Cortex-M4 target built from the workspace source with clang for thumbv7m-none-eabi and linked with ld.lld
hardware fault record captured from the running target, carrying the stacked frame plus CFSR, HFSR, MMFAR, BFAR and EXC_RETURN
matching ELF with symbols shipped next to the record it produced
diagnosis.json derived from the record and the ELF symbol table
repaired source, rebuilt with a fresh seed and executed on the target

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The diagnosis reports the recorded CFSR/HFSR values and the individual status bits they carry, identifies which fault address registers are valid, and does not claim an address from a register the core marked invalid.

The stacked PC and LR are resolved against faults/fault-1.elf to a named function and call site, and the cause is attributed to the configuration or code the board applied rather than to a defective MCU.
The diagnosis states whether the fault is precise or imprecise and what that implies about whether the recorded instruction is the cause, rather than assuming the faulting line is the defect.
The repaired source is rebuilt with a fresh seed and executed on the target, the original fault signature is absent, and the packet path publishes the checksum derived from that seed.

requiredEvidence: board and MCU identity, image hash, and the ELF that matches the record
raw captured record with decoded fault status and address-validity fields
stacked PC and LR resolved to named symbols in the matching ELF
stated precision class for the fault and the cause it implies
target before/after reproduction of the packet path
